title: Aircraft Positioning Instance
description: Schema for an aircraft positioning problem instance

min_separation.description: Tow-in/tow-out time epsilon: minimum separation between consecutive aircraft at the same position and safety margin in the blocking conditions

mu.description: Optional paper-#2 parameter: minimum inter-job pause when used as a Mode-(B) window for a neighbouring access manoeuvre. Default 1.0 day if absent. Ignored by paper-#1 (aircraft-level) code.

delta.description: Optional paper-#2 parameter: working time added to an interruptible job each time it is paused to allow a Mode-(C) access manoeuvre. Default 2.0 days if absent. Ignored by paper-#1 (aircraft-level) code.

eta.description: Optional paper-#2 parameter: time granularity for strict inequalities (e.g. one day). Default 1.0 if absent. Ignored by paper-#1 (aircraft-level) code.

positions.description: List of position identifiers available in the hangar

blocking_arcs.description: Pairs of positions where the front position blocks access to the rear position

aircrafts.description: List of aircraft to be scheduled

earliest_start.description: Earliest time at which work on this aircraft can begin

target_finish.description: Target time by which all work on this aircraft should be completed

jobs.description: List of jobs (work tasks) to be scheduled across aircraft

aircraft_id.description: Identifier of the aircraft this job belongs to

duration.description: Duration of the job in time units

is_first.description: True if this is the first job in the sequence for its aircraft

is_last.description: True if this is the last job in the sequence for its aircraft

interruptible.description: Optional paper-#2 flag: true if the job can be paused to allow a Mode-(C) blocking manoeuvre on a neighbouring rear position. Default false if absent. Ignored by paper-#1 (aircraft-level) code.

job_precedences.description: Ordering constraints between jobs within each aircraft, in increasing task order

before.description: Job that must be completed before the other

after.description: Job that must start after the other is complete
